transcript:
User: yeah.
Agent: Hey, I’m Linda with Dialux — what made you call in today?
User: dunno, whatever's fine.
Agent: Gotcha, sounds like you’re just feeling it out a bit.  

When you think about your business calls, are you ever worried that you or your team might be missing calls from customers when you’re busy or after hours?
User: maybe. dunno, sometimes.
Agent: Totally fair, sounds like it happens here and there but it’s not something you’re tracking closely.  

When a call *does* slip through the cracks—goes to voicemail or rings out—what usually happens next: do people tend to leave a message, or do they just move on to someone else?
User: maybe. dunno. sometimes leave. sometimes not.
Agent: Got it, so it’s kind of a coin flip whether they stick with you or go elsewhere.  

When those calls come in after you’ve closed for the day, where do they go right now — straight to voicemail, an answering service, or just ring out?
User: dunno. voicemail, maybe. depends.
Agent: Yeah, makes sense — sounds like there’s not really a set system right now.  

So just so I’m not wasting your time… are you actually taking customer calls for a business, or is this more of a general “just checking things out” kind of call?
User: dunno. maybe checking. whatever's fine.
Agent: Totally okay to just be checking things out.  

So I don’t spin this in the wrong direction—do you actually have a business that gets incoming customer calls, or not really?
User: dunno. maybe. sometimes. whatever's fine.
Agent: Gotcha, sounds like you’re just casually poking around and not really looking for anything specific right now.  

If you *did* decide to get serious about this later, would it be more about getting more customers from missed calls, or improving customer service for the ones you already have?
User: dunno. maybe both. whatever works. not serious yet. maybe later.
Agent: Totally fair, sounds like this is more “future idea” than “right now” for you.  

Since you’re not serious yet, do you want me to just give you a quick one-liner on what we help with so you know whether it’s worth revisiting later, or would you rather leave it here for now?
User: whatever. maybe later. dunno. sure, one-liner's fine.
Agent: Got it.  

So, in one line: we stop businesses from losing money on missed calls by automatically answering, qualifying the caller, and booking the appointment or taking the message when no one’s available.  

If you ever *do* get more serious later, do you already have a type of business in mind, or is that still up in the air too?
User: dunno, up in the air. whatever works later, maybe.
Agent: Totally makes sense, sounds like it’s all pretty up in the air for now.  

Since you’re only “maybe later,” do you want me to stop here and let you get back to your day, and you can just keep us in mind if missed calls ever become a real issue?
User: yeah, maybe. whatever's fine. sure, keep in mind.
Agent: Got it, we’ll leave it there for now — if missed calls ever start costing you customers, you’ll know this is the kind of thing we help fix so those callers turn into actual opportunities instead of slipping away. Thanks for hanging with me for a bit today, and feel free to call back anytime if it becomes more of a priority — have a good one!
